sections.h2: What hospital queue management software does
paras: Hospital queue management software replaces the token pad and the corridor headcount with a live, ordered queue for each doctor. A walk-in gets a token at the desk, a booked patient is checked in against their appointment, and both appear in the doctor's queue in the order the hospital has chosen. In HIMS this is built into the OPD module rather than sold as a separate token machine.

Because the token is attached to a registered patient, calling the next token opens the patient's record for the doctor. The waiting count per doctor sits on the OPD dashboard for the front desk, and the patient portal lets a patient see their booking. The queue is not a display gimmick; it is the order in which records reach the consulting room.

sections.h2: A token is only useful if the doctor, the desk and the patient see the same number.
sections.lead: Most OPD friction is not the wait itself. It is not knowing where you are in the wait.

items.p: Appointments on a sheet and walk-ins on a pad, merged by whoever is standing at the door.

items.h: Doctor blind to the waiting room
items.p: The consultant does not know whether six or sixteen patients are waiting and paces the morning by guesswork.
A patient steps out for a test and their number is lost; another is called twice by mistake.

items.h: The token is not the record
items.p: Calling number 14 tells the doctor nothing about who number 14 is or what they came for.
A patient asks how long; the desk says soon, because there is no count to look at.

items.q: Is this a token display system?
items.a: It is the queue behind the display. HIMS issues and orders tokens per doctor and shows waiting counts on the OPD dashboard. If you want the queue shown on a screen in the waiting area, describe the setup on a call and it is scoped with the project.

items.q: How are appointments and walk-ins ordered?
items.a: Both feed the same queue for the doctor. The rule for how a checked-in appointment is placed relative to walk-in tokens is set to your hospital's policy during setup.

items.q: Do patients get updates on their phone?
items.a: The patient app and portal let patients book and see their appointment. Notification workflows beyond that are discussed on the call so nothing is promised that your setup does not include.

items.q: Can a token be moved or cancelled?
items.a: Yes. The desk can move a token later in the queue when a patient steps out, transfer it to another doctor in the same department, or cancel it if the patient leaves.

items.q: Does it work for departments as well as individual doctors?
items.a: Yes. Queues can be per doctor or per department, following the doctor rosters, so a general medicine queue can be shared by whichever consultants are on duty. See doctor management software.
